title: How to use VS Code for IT project coordinators on Mac: a guide

description: Learn how to use VS Code for IT project coordinators on Mac to manage documentation, track tasks, and organize project files efficiently.
targetKeyword: vs code for it project coordinators on mac
intro: Using VS Code for IT project coordinators on Mac helps you manage project documentation, track task files, and organize technical requirements in one place. While often seen as a developer tool, its robust file management and text editing features make it an excellent hub for managing project-related data.
tldr: VS Code is a powerful text editor that works well for managing project documentation and technical notes.
Use File > Open Folder to manage your project files as a cohesive workspace.
Install extensions to add functionality like Markdown previewing or Git integration.
Use the Command Palette (Cmd + Shift + P) to find any setting or feature quickly.
Lazur helps you interact with VS Code hands-free by pointing at menus and explaining features.

blocks.text: The most common mistake new users make is opening individual files. When you work on a project, you need context. Always use File > Open Folder to load your entire project directory. This allows VS Code to index your files and provide better search results across your documentation.

items: Select File > Open Folder from the top menu.
Your files appear in the sidebar on the left.

blocks.text: You can save hours by mastering a few key shortcuts. The Command Palette is your best friend. Press ⌘ ⇧ P to open it. Type any command to find it instantly. This removes the need to hunt through menus.

blocks.caption: Keyboard shortcuts for VS Code on Mac.

blocks.text: VS Code is built for Markdown files. These files are perfect for project plans, meeting notes, and status reports. They are plain text, meaning they are easy to version control. Click the Open Preview to the Side button in the top right to see your formatted document while you type.
If your preview stops working, check your extensions. You might need a Markdown support extension if you are using specific custom formatting.
blocks.title: Preview Tip

blocks.text: Why IT project coordinators use VS Code

You likely manage many files. VS Code handles large projects better than standard text editors. It also integrates with Git. If your team uses Git for project files, you can commit changes directly from the Source Control tab.

items: Preview mode: Files in italics are temporary. Double-click them to pin them permanently.
Missing features: VS Code is an editor, not an IDE out of the box. Install extensions for specific file types.
UI clutter: If you hide a panel, use View > Appearance > Reset View Locations to bring it back.

blocks.text: You can change how VS Code looks and feels. Access settings by pressing ⌘ ,. You can change your color theme, font size, or cursor behavior. If you want to sync these settings across multiple Macs, use the Settings Sync feature.

faq.question: Can I use VS Code for project management?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use it to manage documentation, track task lists in Markdown, and view project files in a structured way.

faq.question: Is VS Code free to use?
faq.answer: Yes, VS Code is a free, open-source editor provided by Microsoft.

faq.question: How do I install extensions?
faq.answer: Click the Extensions icon in the sidebar (or press ⌘ ⇧ X) and search for the extension you need.

faq.question: What if I lose my menu bars?
faq.answer: Go to View > Appearance > Reset View Locations to restore the default layout.
